systems.description: Faces of the western and southern ramparts of the citadel
Annexe rampart and the house block north of it
House walls inside the citadel that run closer to the plan's north than the ramparts
Exposed ramparts, revetment and entrance walls on the sketch plan

main_system_reason: The citadel ramparts are the longest straight lines at the site and frame the whole settlement; the annexe rampart and houses follow nearly the same direction.
notes: We measured two plans from Joshi's 1990 report: the large fold-out plan of structures (Fig. 8) and the smaller sketch plan of structures (Fig. 4). Both carry an arrow lettered only N, so the north reference is unspecified. On Fig. 8 the faces of the western and southern ramparts of the citadel, the annexe rampart and the annexe houses agree closely, and the houses of blocks 2 and 3 inside the citadel run several degrees closer to the plan's north than the ramparts around them. Fig. 4 gives the same rampart lines turned about five degrees closer to north than Fig. 8. The two figures come from the same excavation, so the difference lies in how north was drawn on one or both of them; Fig. 4 is a sketch with a short freehand arrow and a frame whose top edge is out of square by about 0.8 deg, so we prefer Fig. 8 and keep Fig. 4 as a separate, weaker witness. Dashed outlines on Fig. 8 (the northern rampart and the outer limits) and the 'conjecture' hatching on Fig. 4 are restorations and were not measured. The conjectural restoration of Period IC (Fig. 9) was not measured.
